idea-plugin.name: Blamely
idea-plugin.description:
Blamely attributes every line of code to AI or human — across inline completions, chat apply, and agent runs. The breakdown appears in the status bar as you work, survives branch switches, and attaches permanently to each commit via git notes.

All data stays on your machine. No account, no telemetry, no network access.

How it works

  1. Record. When an AI tool edits a file, its hook calls blamely record <tool>.
  2. Watch. The daemon also tails Cursor logs, Copilot transcripts, and filesystem activity.
  3. Attribute. On every commit, the global post-commit hook diffs the commit against stored edits and writes per-line attribution.
  4. Report. The IDE plugin reads those notes back into the status bar, tool window, and gutter.

After each commit

A clear AI vs Human bar prints in your terminal immediately after git commit:

AI 72% (18)  [████████████████████████████░░░░░░░░░░░░]  Human 28% (7)
  claude  12 lines  (claude-opus-4-6) — 4200 in / 890 out tok
  cursor   6 lines  (composer-1)      — 1100 in / 340 out tok

Status bar

The status bar widget shows live AI / Human metrics for the active file:

AI: 751 © 24 = 98%  |  Human: 12 © 3 = 2%  |  claude-opus-4-6

© = characters, = = lines. Click to open the full panel.

Changes tool window

The Blamely → Changes tab shows per-file AI / Human breakdown for all uncommitted work on the current branch, with a visual progress bar per file and a session summary at the bottom.

History tool window

The Blamely → History tab shows AI vs Human share across past commits — total lines, per-model breakdown, commit table with timing, and a segmented bar. Example:

482 AI lines · 40.2%  |  716 Human · 59.8%
18 commits · 44 files · Coding: 32m 17s · AI wait: 50s

#1  claude-opus-4-6  135 lines · 28.0% · 1 commit
#2  cursor-composer   82 lines · 17.0% · 3 commits

Example report.yml (attached to each commit)

scope: "this_commit"
generated_at: "2026-03-05T00:43:50Z"
branch: "main"
commit_hash: "3317ed295e"
commit_message: "[AI-assisted] feat: update analysis"

ai_sources:
  - claude
  - cursor

files:
  - path: "src/utils/parser.ts"
    source: "claude"
    model: "claude-opus-4-6"
    ai_lines_added: 22
    human_lines_added: 65
    percentage: "40.0%"

Requirements — Install the CLI first

macOS

curl -sSL https://blamely.ai/blamely-mac-install.sh | bash

Linux

curl -sSL https://blamely.ai/blamely-linux-install.sh | bash

Windows (PowerShell)

powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command "irm https://blamely.ai/blamely-windows-install.bat | iex"

Installers are idempotent — safe to re-run after adding a new AI tool. Verify:

blamely status    # daemon health + detected tools
blamely doctor    # full self-check

Full guide: blamely.ai

Features

  • Line-level blame — Gutter icons + tooltips (AI vs human per line)
  • Status bar widget — Live AI / Human chars, lines, percentage, active model
  • Changes tool window — Per-file breakdown for uncommitted work on current branch
  • History tool window — Per-model stats, commit table, timing across past commits
  • Git notes — report.yml on every commit via refs/notes/blamely
  • Pre-commit / pre-push hooks — Survive plugin upgrades via stable runner scripts
  • Branch-scoped sessions — State under .git/blamely/<branch>/
  • Actions — Generate Report, Show Blame, Install/Restore Hook, Show Commit Report, Push AI Notes
  • VS Code compatible — Same .git/blamely layout; both IDEs share attribution data
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.8.5

  • Editing very large files no longer freezes the IDE — a small change to a very large file could make the plugin use a huge amount of memory and bring the IDE to a halt. It now stays light however large the file is, and very large changes are attributed more accurately too.
  • Git worktrees are fully supported — if you work on several branches side by side in separate worktrees, each one now shows its own correct record of who wrote what.
  • Blamely now works with OpenCode — code written by OpenCode (V1 and V2) is now tracked and credited to it.
  • git push no longer waits for Blamely — sharing attribution with your team now happens in the background, and a push that fails no longer loses your in-progress attribution.
  • Commits are fast again in long-used repositories — tidying up old records could add tens of seconds to every commit, especially on Windows. It now takes a moment.
  • A new look — Blamely has a new logo.

1.8.2

  • Pasting no longer freezes the IDE — every paste of more than a few characters made Blamely run several git commands before the editor was allowed to respond, and a multi-cursor paste, or the automatic reformat that follows one, multiplied that by every insertion point. Blamely now gets the same information without running anything at all, and does the rest out of your way. Typing is lighter too: the plugin was copying the whole file three times on every keystroke, even when nothing needed those copies.
  • Branching before you commit no longer credits the AI's work to you — working on your main branch and creating a branch when it is time to commit (git checkout -b my-feature) quietly lost the entire session's AI attribution, and the commit reported every AI-written line as hand-written. It is now carried across the branch you made, and the gutter is right straight away rather than only after the commit.
  • Attribution reaches your remote again after the first clash — once a teammate's breakdown had arrived at the remote before yours, or your own rebase had rewritten yours, every send after that was refused in silence and your records stayed on your machine. Both sides are now brought together and sent.
  • Blamely now tells you when a project switches it off — a project that manages its own git hooks (Husky, lefthook, pre-commit) takes over the setting Blamely depends on, and Blamely then records nothing at all there. blamely doctor now reports it and tells you what to do.

1.8.1

  • Attribution written on a detached HEAD is no longer lost — while you were on a detached HEAD (during a rebase, or after checking out a commit directly), the IDE saved your in-progress attribution to a different folder than the one Blamely reads at commit time, so that work was credited to nobody. Both now agree.
  • Blamely uses far less CPU while you type — the plugin re-read your whole project's attribution on every keystroke, and ran git twice every three seconds just to notice commits, plus twice more each time it saved your in-progress attribution. Commits, branch switches and stashes are now noticed the moment git writes them — instantly instead of up to three seconds later — and the re-read happens when the data actually changes rather than while you're still typing.
  • Switching tabs is quick again — opening a file used to re-read attribution for the entire project. It now reads only the files you can see.
  • Leftover Blamely processes — when recording lines an AI tool had deleted, the plugin started a helper it never waited for and never limited, so a stuck one stayed running until you closed the IDE. They now give up after ten seconds, and no more than a few run at a time.

1.7.0

  • A setting for when the AI/Human breakdown doesn't show up — on very large projects, or slow and company-managed machines, Blamely could give up reading your history before it finished and leave the gutter and tool window empty. It now waits up to a minute instead of a few seconds, and you can raise that further under Settings → Tools → Blamely → Authorship CLI timeout.
  • The plugin ships fully readable — all code-scrambling was removed, so the published plugin is exactly the public source and your security team can verify what runs in your IDE.

1.6.9

  • Attribution survives cherry-pick, squash, and stash — reorganizing your history keeps the AI-vs-human credit on each line instead of resetting it to Human.
  • The gutter and tool window keep up with your work — Blamely now notices file and branch changes as they happen, so the AI/Human view refreshes on its own instead of lagging behind.
  • Same behaviour as the VS Code extension — attribution, the status bar, and the Changes and History views now match what the VS Code extension shows for the same project.

1.6.4

  • AI work no longer slips to "Human" — brand-new files an assistant creates (for example a generated package.json) are now credited to the assistant instead of falling back to Human.
  • Attribution survives history changes — amending, rebasing, or re-committing a change keeps its AI/human credit instead of resetting it to Human.
  • Lighter and faster with the editor open — background refreshes now run one at a time, so Blamely no longer piles up dozens of helper processes that competed for resources and slowed things down.
  • Just one background helper — only a single Blamely daemon runs at a time; duplicates exit instead of accumulating.
  • Quicker gutter on large repositories — per-file attribution now reads commit history in fewer steps, so the gutter fills in faster.

1.6.3

  • More accurate when AI and your edits mix — when an assistant rewrites a file you'd just edited by hand, your lines stay yours and only the assistant's lines are credited to it.
  • Works across your whole workspace — AI and human changes are now tracked in every Git repository in the workspace, not just the first one found.
  • New files show up right away — brand-new files appear in the gutter the moment you start writing, without staging them in Git first.
  • A friendly nudge for new projects — open a folder that isn't a Git repository yet and Blamely offers to set it up.
  • Clearer status bar — the AI and human summary now leads with the percentage.
  • A cleaner, consistent gutter — the AI and human markers share the same crisp sizing across VS Code and JetBrains.

1.6.0

  • Status bar count now matches the gutter — the AI/Human status bar widget previously summed every tracked file across the project and counted blank lines, while the gutter shows only the active file and skips blanks. The widget now reports the active file only, resolved exactly like the gutter (repo-relative path + live blank-line check), so the number equals the icons in front of you.

action.description: Refresh gutter attribution for active editor
